title: Steering Strength x Calibration Collapse: Does Pushing a Concept Wreck the Model's Uncertainty?

original_idea.body: Steering may sharpen a behavior while destroying calibration, so confidence-gated safety mechanisms break; measure accuracy vs ECE across strengths.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to confidence-gated safety mechanisms breaking, but link to a concrete catastrophic scenario is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Steering sweep + ECE/accuracy on a multiple-choice benchmark with logprobs; accessible to a motivated beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single experiment: sweep strength, measure accuracy vs ECE; clean success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public benchmarks, no internal access; a measurement labs are unlikely to prioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on one open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Calibration effects of steering are plausibly touched on; the decoupling-rate angle may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Steering side-effects on calibration may be partly studied but the decoupling-rate framing could be open.
